messages_body:
Hi Jamie + Tom,

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and proposed technical pathway so we can move to a scoped POC. I captured the pain, the success criteria you shared, and suggested next steps below. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points you described:
- Current triage assistant returns inconsistent prioritization for urgent referrals (precision at top-k is low).
- Latency spikes on peak hours when running models in-house; cost of overprovisioned GPUs is a concern.
- Difficulty adding structured outputs into downstream EHR fields (need deterministic JSON schemas).

Goals for the POC (agreed):
1) Demonstrate 95%+ top-1 relevance on a 500-case test set for triage labels (embeddings + rerank).
2) End-to-end latency below 450ms p95 for classification/structured extraction in production-like load.
3) Delivery of a function-calling + streaming pipeline that emits a validated JSON payload for EHR ingestion.

Technical pathway we propose:
- Phase A (week 1): Connector + sample dataset ingest (you provide 500 de-identified cases).
- Phase B (week 2–3): SDK integration for embeddings + rerank; run offline evals and iterate.
- Phase C (week 4): Deploy a streaming inference route with function calling for structured outputs; run load test.

Key asks from HealthPath:
- Confirm dataset delivery window (CSV or NDJSON) and an example EHR schema.
- Which internal environments should we target for latency tests (us-east-1 and on-prem in their NYC datacenter?).

Attached is a short integration checklist that maps SDK changes we expect on your side (client config, auth, and the function-calling wrapper). Ben will follow up with a minimal example payload for your engineering team.

Next steps:
- Jamie: share test dataset by EOD Thu (2026-08-31) or let us know constraints.
- Ben: send example SDK patch + sample curl and streaming payload (ETA tomorrow).
- Hannah: I'll draft SOW and security responses and loop procurement when scope is confirmed.

Thanks again — excited to move this forward.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

On Aug 28, 2026, at 3:04 PM, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [quoted initial recap]

Jamie/Tom — quick technical note from our infra/SDK lead: Marcus is cc'd here. Two clarifications on the engineering approach:

1) Embeddings + Rerank: we'll use embedding vectors for candidate retrieval (faiss-style index) followed by a lightweight neural reranker served via Redwood dedicated route. For the POC we recommend an n_cand=50 retrieval window and a reranker tuned for precision@1. We can tune for recall if you prefer.

2) Function calling & structured outputs: Redwood supports two patterns — (A) synchronous function calling where model emits a JSON blob validated by our schema layer; (B) streaming function calls where partial outputs are emitted as tokens and validated at the edge. For HealthPath's EHR ingestion, pattern (A) is simplest and most deterministic; pattern (B) can reduce perceived latency for longer docs but requires incremental validation on your ingest side.

3) Latency budgeting: to reach p95 <450ms we recommend the following knobs: smaller batching window (10ms), prefix KV caching for repeating prompt headers, and 8-bit quantized weights on the reranker. We'll include suggested config in the sample patch.

Example minimal streaming payload (high level):
- client -> POST /v1/stream?route=hp-triage
- headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- body: {
  \"input\": \"<note text>\",
  \"max_tokens\": 256,
  \"function_schema\": \"hp_triage_v1\"
}

We'll send a ready-to-run snippet and a small test harness that uses mock EHR writes to validate structured JSON.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
